cases.description: The parent schema's schema node contains a "type" field with the textual value "object". The method should return the string "object".
The parent schema's schema node does not contain a "type" field. The method should fall through the if‑statement and return null.

If getParentSchema() returns null, the call to getParentSchema().getSchemaNode() triggers a NullPointerException. This test confirms the current implementation does not guard against a null parent schema.
The parent schema's schema node contains a "type" field whose value is a numeric node (123). The method should return the numeric value as its string representation "123".
The parent schema's schema node contains a "type" field whose value is a boolean node (true). The method should return the boolean value as its string representation "true".

The parent schema's schema node contains a "type" field whose value is an array node (e.g., ["string", "null"]). For non‑textual nodes Jackson's asText() returns an empty string, so the method should return "".
The parent schema's schema node contains a "type" field whose value is an explicit JSON null. Jackson's NullNode.asText() yields the string "null", which the method should return.
The parent schema's schema node contains a "type" field whose value is an object node. Since the node is not textual, asText() returns an empty string; the method should therefore return "".

The parent schema's getSchemaNode() returns null. Attempting to call get("type") on a null reference triggers a NullPointerException. This test verifies that the method does not guard against a null schema node.
